bull_case: 유리한 사업·자본배분 가정이 유지되면 기준 점수보다 높은 결과가 가능하다.
bear_case: 성장·마진·자본배분이 정상화되고 핵심 불확실성이 불리하게 전개되면 기준 점수보다 낮아질 수 있다.
thesis: Berkshire is not a disruption-led investment. Its edge is capital allocation, insurance float and decentralized operating ownership rather than a single technology adoption curve.

evidence.claim: Berkshire's businesses span insurance, energy, rail, manufacturing, service and retail.
OxyChem was acquired for about $9.4B on January 2, 2026.
Taylor Morrison was acquired in July 2026 for about $6.8B equity value.

counterevidence: BHE grid and renewable investments can benefit from electrification.
GEICO can use data/telematics and digital distribution to improve economics.
Acquisition optionality can shift Berkshire into new value pools.
unknowns: Quantified returns from technology investment inside major subsidiaries.
Evidence that a Berkshire platform creates cross-subsidiary network effects.
falsifiers: A subsidiary creates a category-defining platform with independent adoption evidence.
Multiple new value pools become material to consolidated earnings.
Technology materially changes consolidated unit economics.

subscores.rationale: Berkshire mainly owns mature businesses; innovation is generally sustaining rather than a 10x cost/performance disruption.
No single Berkshire-wide adoption S-curve defines the thesis.
Diversified acquisitions create options but do not establish a new value-chain standard.
